chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about four persons who killed a man: a slave, a free man, a free woman, and a mukātab who had paid half of his mukātabah. He said: “The diyah is upon them: upon the free man is one quarter of the diyah, and upon the free woman is one quarter of the diyah. As for the slave, his master is to be given the choice: if he wishes, he pays on his behalf; and if he wishes, he surrenders him in his entirety; his family is not liable for anything. As for the mukātab, half of the quarter is upon him from his property, and half of the quarter is upon those who contracted his mukātabah. That quarter is so because half of him has been emancipated.”

key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: was emancipated, indicating partial freedom as the basis of partial liability
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for unlawful killing
key_terms.الْحُرَّةِ: the free woman whose liability is assigned as one quarter of the diyah
key_terms.الْحُرِّ: the free man whose liability is assigned as one quarter of the diyah
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: the slave, regarding whom the master is given a legal choice
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master, who may either pay on his behalf or surrender him
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: a contractually emancipating slave who has paid part of his emancipation price
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: his manumission contract, of which half has been fulfilled

ai.seo_question: How is the diyah divided when a free man, a free woman, a slave, and a partially emancipated mukātab jointly commit a killing?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal ruling for diyah when four different types of persons jointly kill one man: a slave, a free man, a free woman, and a partially emancipated mukātab. It specifies how liability is apportioned according to each person's legal status, including the master's option regarding the slave and the divided responsibility of the mukātab whose emancipation is half complete.
